---
title: "Plots"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5,
                      dpi = 96)
```

Every result object has a `plot()` method that returns a ggplot, so the
display can be modified with the usual `+` and saved with
`ggplot2::ggsave()`. The colours and shapes are the same on every display:
providers **above** the reference in orange triangles, **below** in blue
squares, **not different** in grey circles, **not tested** in light grey
crosses.

```{r setup}
library(pprof)
d <- sim_kecc(n_providers = 150, provider_size = c(12, 100), seed = 11)
pd <- pp_data(d, y = "y", x = c("x1", "x2", "x3"), provider = "provider",
              patient = "patient", message = FALSE)
fit <- fit_logistic_fe(pd)
tst <- test(fit, statistic = "wald", variance = "robust", null_model = "empirical")
```

## Caterpillar plot

Every provider's estimate and interval in order of the estimate, coloured
by its flag, with the reference as a dashed line. The intervals are those
of the test (calibrated when the test was), so an interval excludes the
reference exactly when the provider is flagged.

```{r}
plot(tst)
plot(tst, highlight = tst$provider[tst$flag == 1][1:3])
```

## Funnel plot

Estimates against precision, with control limits from the same test as the
flags: a provider outside the limits is a flagged provider, nothing else.
For a test with standard errors the x axis is $1 / se^2$ and the limits
are $\theta_0 \pm c \cdot se$ at the test's level (solid) and at 0.998
(dashed); when the test was calibrated with an empirical null there is one
panel per null group, each with its own limits.

```{r}
plot(tst, type = "funnel")
```

For the Poisson tests of a Cox fit the x axis is the expected number of
events and the limits are the counts the test flags at every expected
count:

```{r}
s <- sim_kecc(n_providers = 120, provider_size = c(15, 80), type = "survival", seed = 3)
ps <- pp_data(s, x = c("x1", "x2", "x3"), provider = "provider", patient = "patient",
              time = "stop", start = "start", event = "event", cutoff = 0, message = FALSE)
cox <- fit_cox(ps)
plot(test(cox, min_expected = 2), type = "funnel")
```

## Flags by provider size

The shares of providers flagged above, below and not different, within
quartiles of provider size and overall. The display behind the empirical
null: under the theoretical null the share of flagged providers grows with
size.

```{r}
plot(test(fit, statistic = "wald", variance = "robust"), type = "bar")
plot(tst, type = "bar")
```

## Observed against expected

A `standardize()` result draws the observed total against the expected one
with the diagonal; pass the test to colour the providers. `type =
"funnel"` draws the ratio against its precision $E^2 / V$: without a test,
with the normal limits of the naive score statistic; with a score test, that
test's own funnel, so that the limits and the colours come from the same
test (a Wald-type test is drawn with `plot(test, type = "funnel")`, above).

```{r}
sm <- standardize(fit)
plot(sm, test = tst)
plot(sm, type = "funnel")
plot(sm, type = "funnel", test = test(fit, statistic = "score", variance = "robust"))
```

## Forest plot of the coefficients

```{r}
plot(summary(fit, test = "robust_wald"))
plot(summary(fit), exponentiate = TRUE)
```

## Null calibration

The statistics against the theoretical and the fitted null, one panel per
size group: the display that shows why an empirical null is needed and
what it fitted.

```{r}
plot(null_model("empirical", test(fit, statistic = "wald", variance = "robust")))
```

## Reliability curve

```{r}
expected <- stats::plogis(stats::median(coef(fit)$gamma) + fit$linear_predictor)
plot(iur("bootstrap", obs = fit$data$y, expected = expected, provider = fit$data$provider,
         n_boot = 50, seed = 1))
```

## Selection paths and cross-validation

```{r}
d6 <- sim_kecc(n_providers = 60, n_covariates = 8, beta = c(0.6, -0.5, 0.4, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
               seed = 4)
pd6 <- pp_data(d6, y = "y", x = paste0("x", 1:8), provider = "provider", patient = "patient",
               message = FALSE)
path <- var_select(pd6, n_lambda = 30)
plot(path)
plot(cv(path, n_folds = 5, seed = 1))
```

## Flags under the alternatives

`flag_stability()` lines up the flags of several tests, for the providers
flagged by at least one of them:

```{r}
st <- flag_stability(
  wald_robust = test(fit, statistic = "wald", variance = "robust"),
  score_robust = test(fit, statistic = "score", variance = "robust"),
  empirical = tst,
  exact = test(fit, statistic = "exact"))
plot(st)
```
